newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends off high, new bond active.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends off high, new bond active.

text.p: Indian call money eased in afternoon trade to end Thursday at 6.5-7.0, up from Wednesday's closing rate of 5.0-5.25 but off a morning high of 7.0-7.5 percent, dealers said.
They said rates eased after fears of a squeeze in funds supply after Wednesday's bond auction receded.
The Reserve Bank of India auctioned federal government bonds worth 30 billion rupees on May 28 and accepted bids for the entire amount. Payment by successful bidders was on Thursday.
"Rates opened up on fears that outflows towards yesterday's bond auction would reduce the funds supply in the market," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
"But by afternoon, it was clear funds were available cheaper and lenders started quoting lower rates," the dealer said.
Dealers said they expected call money rates to drop further in the next two days.
"Call money should trade around 5.0-6.0 percent by Saturday given the current liquidity scenario," said a dealer.
Dealers said trade in government securities was active but was largly restricted to the 12.14 percent 2000 bond auctioned on Wednesday and treasury bills.
"The latest bond was much in demand," said a dealer. "It started trading at par but improved to 100.10 rupees by close."

Dealers said prices of other securities rose slightly, with the 13.05 percent 2007 moving up to 100.95 rupees from its last traded 100.87, 12.50 percent 2004 to 99.60 from 99.50 and 12.69 percent 2002 to 100.45 from 100.36.
The April 24, 1998 treasury bill traded steady at 9.5 percent, dealers said.
